record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n+1, 3n+1) for n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
With T (n) = T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1) with n >= 1, it appears that T (n) has no prime factor greater than or equal to 4n.
Problem 9: Find a formula governing T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1). See OEIS entry A364481.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular grid in the plane. For positive integers $a,b$, the $(a,b)$-benzel is a centrally symmetric hexagonal region defined as follows: take the regular triangular lattice and cut out a hexagonal benzel-shaped region whose boundary alternates between sides of length $a$ and $b$ in a fixed cyclic pattern, producing a region tileable by unit triangles. A "stone" is a trimer (a connected shape of three unit triangles) shaped like a half-hexagon; there are two stone orientations called the right stone and the left stone. A "bone" is a trimer consisting of three unit triangles in a straight line; bones come in three orientations corresponding to the three lattice directions.

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, define $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ to be the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel by prototiles drawn from a subset of the six trimers, where: the right stone is allowed iff $i=1$, the left stone is allowed iff $j=1$, and exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations are allowed (with the choice of which $k$ orientations not affecting the count by symmetry, up to relabeling).

Let $T(n) := T_{112}(3n+1,\,3n+1)$ for $n\ge 1$, counting tilings of the $(3n+1,3n+1)$-benzel using both stones together with exactly two of the three bone orientations.

Find a closed-form formula (or generating function / explicit product formula) for $T(n)$ as a function of $n\ge 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open enumeration question. The associated integer sequence is recorded in the OEIS (A364481), and empirical observations suggest the values have no prime factor at least 4n, but no closed-form formula appears to have been established. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Jim Propp's Benzel Tilings Site
status_evidence.snippet: Active research page on benzel tilings listing trimer-cover enumeration problems.
status_evidence.claim: The benzel-tiling enumeration problems including the T112 case are listed as ongoing research questions.

status_evidence.title: A Pentagonal Number Theorem for Tribone Tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Pentagonal number theorem for tribone tilings of benzels, addresses a different subcase.
status_evidence.claim: Related benzel tilings have been solved in special cases (tribones) but not the two-bone-orientation T112 case.
